topic: Rungraph 2026: Ask Your Agent What Happened in a Run with Interactive Graphs

key_points: One command (npx rungraph) converts every agent session already on disk into an interactive graph: orchestrator, subagents, and tool calls as nodes; spawn/return edges; human interventions (permission denials, interrupts) marked on the path
Works retroactively across Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, opencode, and Cursor — no hooks, no wrappers, no telemetry
MCP server: 'Ask your agent what happened' — tools list_runs / get_graph / find_nodes / get_detail / focus_nodes light up the exact nodes the answer is about in the open dashboard
Signal strip flags retry storms, unresolved errors, interventions, outliers, and course changes; zero-height on a clean run
Live growth: a run happening right now grows live as the agent works; replay bar scrubs through the run
Export/share bundles (.rungraph) with secret redaction; blocks on high-confidence secrets (AWS keys, GitHub/Slack/API tokens)
Coverage: reports how many records it read vs. couldn't interpret (transcript formats undocumented)
No network use — fully local
Searchable team log for AI coding agent sessions — a team visibility layer over agent conversations
Positions agent-run visibility as a team/collaboration problem, not just individual debugging
Contrast: rungraph focuses on graph structure + MCP-driven interrogation; agentlore focuses on searchability/team indexing
LangChain's SmithDB positions agent observability as needing a purpose-built data layer
Enterprise LLM tracing/observability trend validates demand for agent-run introspection
Contrast: centralized/traced observability vs. rungraph's zero-instrumentation local replay of existing transcripts
Grafana agent observability for Hermes Agent — bringing agent runs into existing dashboards
Shows the observability ecosystem is racing to ingest agent run data into standard tools
Contrast: Grafana ingestion/aggregation vs. rungraph's graph-native interactive visualization + MCP query
2026 landscape: multiple terminal agents (Goose, Claude Code, opencode, Pi) coexist and fragment run/session formats
Multi-agent heterogeneity is exactly the problem rungraph's vendor-neutral IR and cross-agent graph solve
Terminal/CLI agents are mainstream in 2026, making run-visualization a real, growing need

stats.fact: rungraph works across five agents — Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, opencode, and Cursor — with a single command and no hooks
A single large agent run graph can exceed 20,000 tokens if fully serialized, motivating narrow-then-pull MCP queries (find_nodes) rather than full graph dumps
Export example: 2 runs, 143 nodes, 12 prompts, 24 files touched in a 412KB .rungraph bundle
rungraph reads Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, opencode, and Cursor session formats from disk; Hermes/opencode/Cursor runs need Node >= 22.13 for the built-in SQLite reader
rungraph was released as a Show HN (Aug 2026) by FayzanMalik, open-source, JavaScript, 24 stars / 2 forks as of research date
Terminal agents were mainstream in 2026 (Goose, Claude Code, opencode, Pi comparisons circulating), fragmenting run/session formats and driving demand for cross-agent run visualization
Transcript formats for coding agents are undocumented and unversioned; rungraph measures 'coverage' (e.g. 'read 95% of this run') and names records it couldn't interpret

angles: 'Ask your agent what happened' — MCP turns a silent transcript into a question-answerable, visual artifact; the graph lights up the nodes the answer references
Zero-instrumentation retroactive visualization: no hooks/wrappers/telemetry, everything already on disk — a different model than tracing/DAG frameworks
The signal strip as 'opinionated observability' — flags retry storms, unresolved errors, interventions, outliers, course changes instead of rendering everything equal
Security angle: export blocks on high-confidence secrets because transcripts log file reads verbatim (agent merely opening .env captures its keys)
Multi-agent, vendor-neutral IR — a Codex run opens identically to a Claude Code run; solves terminal-agent fragmentation
Replay + focus_nodes deep links shareable into PRs — making agent runs a reviewable, collaborative artifact
Hermes Agent native support makes this directly relevant to our own pipeline tooling
